:::{#thm-negate-existential}
#### De Morgan's law for an existential quantifier

For a [set](#def-set) $S$ and a [predicate](#def-predicate) $P(x)$
whose [domain of discourse](#def-domain-of-discourse) is $S$:

$$
\neg (\exists x \in S, P(x)) \equiv \forall x \in S, \neg P(x)
$$

:::

::: proof

By the definition of the [existential quantifier](#def-existential-quantifier),
$\exists x \in S, P(x)$ is false
exactly when $P(x)$ is false for every $x$ in $S$.
By the definition of the [universal quantifier](#def-universal-quantifier),
that is exactly when $\forall x \in S, \neg P(x)$ is true.

:::
